messages:
alex: CI red on PR #6123 — image publish step failing with HTTP 431 Request Header Fields Too Large after I added a long build-arg (base64 key). Happening in our CI during the push stage. Log snippet below:

alex: ```
[push] PUT /v2/org/service/blobs/uploads/?digest=sha256:... 431
http: request header too large
headers: Authorization: <very-long-token>, X-Registry-Auth: <base64...>
BuildKit: pushing layers... failed
```

dena: link to PR? is this our registry or a partner one?

alex: https://github.com/redwood-inference/service/pull/6123
it's our internal registry behind nginx + auth proxy (region-eu). Last green on main: d4f2a9c

sam: can you try a rerun? sometimes transient auth tokens cause weird header growth. ci-bot, rerun job? :eyes:

ci-bot: job rerun queued: https://ci.internal/jobs/98765 (requested by sam)

alex: rerun 98765 shows same 431 at the same step, not transient.

olga: did the Dockerfile change add new build-arg with a huge value? Buildkit passes that in X-Registry-Auth sometimes if inline cache or exporting credentials used.

alex: yes I added BUILD_SECRET_BASE64 as a --build-arg (auto-generated, ~9kB). I thought it was fine since it's only during build.

ryan: nginx will 431 on headers > large_client_header_buffers. Two options: shrink header (avoid inline base64 in headers) or bump nginx buffer but that's not ideal. Can you reproduce with curl directly to registry to confirm header size is the issue?

alex: tried curl to the same endpoint with the same Authorization header and it returns 431 too. snippet:

alex: ```
curl -v -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer <long-token>" \
  -H "X-Registry-Auth: <very-long-base64>" \
  "https://registry.internal/v2/org/service/blobs/uploads/"
# -> HTTP/1.1 431 Request Header Fields Too Large
```

tanvi: quick workaround: avoid pushing the inline cache to registry: set BUILDKIT_INLINE_CACHE=0 or disable cache export so X-Registry-Auth shrinks. Also consider passing secrets via file mounts or BuildKit secrets (not as build-arg).

sam: another test: try kaniko or skopeo to push layers without the big header to see if it's buildkit-specific.

alex: trying a repro on my laptop with BUILDKIT_INLINE_CACHE=0 now. will report back.

(20m later)

alex: update — setting BUILDKIT_INLINE_CACHE=0 on CI made the push succeed. artifacts pushed, job passed. Seems inline cache export encoded into X-Registry-Auth caused header to balloon.

olga: cool. root cause narrowed: inline cache export + large build-arg ended up in registry auth header (encoded). We should avoid large build args and use build secrets or env files.

ryan: ops note: we shouldn't widen nginx buffers unless absolutely necessary. That masks the payload problem. Filed infra task to add a short paragraph to eng-infra runbook about large build args + inline cache -> 431: https://infra.internal/tasks/INF-4212

dena: alex — can you update the PR to remove the big build-arg and use a secret file mount + add a short comment in the Dockerfile? then we can close this thread.

alex: will do. thanks all for quick triage :thumbsup:

tanvi: marking as resolved unless you hit it again.

alex: closing — re-ran full pipeline, green. leaving notes in PR and linking INF-4212.
